title: Athanasius (c. 296–373)
hookLine: exiled again and again, he held that Christ is truly God

cards: Night, in a church in Alexandria. The people are keeping vigil with their bishop. Soldiers surround the building, and then they break in.
In his own account, the bishop doesn't bolt for the back door. He stays in his chair.

He tells the deacon to begin a psalm, and the people answer the refrain, for his mercy endureth for ever, while they slip out ahead of him. Only when most are safe does he slip away himself, into the dark.
His name is Athanasius, and it isn't the first time he's had to run.

teach.b: First, who he was: bishop of Alexandria, a great city of the early Church, when emperors took a close interest in what bishops taught.

Athanasius held one thing with his whole life: that Jesus Christ, the Son, is truly God, not the highest of creatures but one in being with the Father. Tomorrow, the argument on the other side. Second, what it cost him.
Emperors sent him away, and sent him away again, to distant cities. He hid in the desert among the monks, who kept him safe, and, tradition says, once in his own father's tomb.
Each time he came back and took up his work, writing letters and books from wherever he was. Third, why it mattered to him.

teach.h: MADE MAN, THAT WE MIGHT BE MADE GOD.
teach.b: In his little book On the Incarnation, he gives the reason in a single sentence: "He was made man that we might be made God."

If the Son were only a creature, Athanasius argued, he couldn't join us to God, because he would be on our side of the line too. Only God could bring us to God. The Catechism of the Catholic Church still quotes that line.
Fourth, the phrase in today's carry. Later generations summed him up in Latin: Athanasius contra mundum, Athanasius against the world.
It's a saying about him, not a slogan he chose, and it can be misheard as stubbornness for its own sake.
For Athanasius, the point was never to win. It was to keep handing on what the Church had confessed, even when it was unpopular, even when it meant sleeping in the desert.
Catholics honor him as a saint and a Doctor of the Church.

how: Catholics honor Saint Athanasius as a bishop and Doctor of the Church, and his teaching that the Son is one in being with the Father is professed in the Creed at Sunday Mass.

games.q: you're the bishop, keeping vigil with your people at night. soldiers break into the church. what do you do?
o: run first, before they reach you.
stay in your chair, keep the psalm going, and leave after your people.
give yourself up on the spot.
games.why: in his own account he stayed seated while the deacon led the psalm and the people slipped out, and only then escaped himself.

practice: Think of something you hold to be true, about faith, fairness or a person, that you don't say out loud because it would cost you a little.
Don't rehearse an argument; ask a gentler question: what would it look like to stand by this, kindly, without needing to win? If you pray, ask for courage and gentleness together.

wordCard.voice: Athanasius. The bishop of Alexandria who, through exile after exile, held that Christ is truly God. Today's word.
